requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** I found no gaps. I did not run the repository validator over the whole tree. I read the code and tests below.

**Implementation**

- `src/rust_coverage.rs` `rust_files` walks the project from the root and collects every `.rs` file.
  - It skips `.git` and `target` directories at any depth.
  - It skips `book`, `evidence`, and `vendor` only when the directory's parent is the project root.
  - Nested directories such as `src/vendor` and `src/book` are still scanned.
  - IO errors during the scan are reported, not swallowed.
- `validate_rust_functions` reads each file and calls `missing_function_references`.
  - A parse failure is pushed as `file:line: cannot parse Rust source: …`, so the file is not silently skipped.
  - Each unreferenced item is reported as `file:line: <kind> <name> has no requirement or example citation`, which gives file, line, kind, and name.
- `missing_function_references` parses with `outline::RUST_PROFILE` (`src/outline/rust.rs`).
  - The profile's `KINDS` list covers `function_item`, `function_signature_item` (trait methods), `struct_item`, `enum_item`, and `union_item`.
  - A comment counts for an item only if the outline assigns it that item as `comment.owner`.
  - The outline assignment follows `requirements.references.outline_comments`. It handles comment runs, trailing comments, inner docs bound to their container, and comments before fields, variants, or attributes falling to the enclosing item.
  - Comments come from the parse tree, not from scanning text. A reference in a string literal therefore does not count, and a reference on an enclosing module or impl block is not credited to the items inside it.
  - A reference is valid only if its role is `impl`, `cite`, or `test` (not a term reference) and its target is a defined requirement or example.
  - Examples missing a requirement `{cite}` or `{test}` are reported separately in `collect_definitions` in `src/evidence.rs`, which implements `requirements.examples.definition`.
- `inspect_repository_with_progress` calls `validate_rust_functions` and adds its errors to the report. All of these functions carry `{impl}` markers for this requirement. `display_path` is a small helper that is also marked.

**Tests**

- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
  - a reference on an enclosing `mod` or `impl` not counting;
  - references in string and raw-string literals not counting;
  - an unknown requirement not counting;
  - a reference in the body counting;
  - a comment run before a blank line counting;
  - trailing-comment ownership;
  - inner doc comments;
  - outer doc comments.
- `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, test helpers, and `{test}` references to both a requirement and a named example.
- `structs_enums_and_unions_need_references_attached_or_inside` covers:
  - structs, enums, and unions;
  - a comment before an attribute, field, or variant belonging to the item;
  - `{cite}` references counting;
  - nested structs.
- `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` checks line numbers after non-ASCII text.
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` covers:
  - exclusions at any depth for `.git` and `target`;
  - root-only exclusions for `book`, `evidence`, and `vendor`, with nested `src/vendor` and `src/book` still scanned;
  - reporting of a parse failure.
- Two integration tests (`tests/authoring_batch.rs`, `tests/commands.rs`) check that parse failures and uncited-function findings reach the CLI output.

**Minor observations (not gaps)**

- No test specifically checks that a `{term}` reference fails to count.
- A reference to an example that is itself invalid still counts for item coverage, but that example is reported as an error elsewhere.

text: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.targets`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
